---
title: Verify webhook signatures
description: Check that a webhook came from your ClipMux server and wasn't changed or replayed, in Node, Python, Go or PHP.
---

Anyone can POST to your webhook URL. Before you trust an event, check its
signature: an HMAC of the timestamp and the body, keyed with your webhook
secret. `clipmuxHandler` and `clipmux.webhooks.verify` do this for you. This
page explains the scheme, and gives tested code for backends in Python, Go
and PHP.

## Before you start

- Your endpoint's secret, `whsec_…`, as `CLIPMUX_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. It's
  shown once, when the endpoint is made.
- Your framework's raw request body: the bytes exactly as they arrived.

## The scheme

Every delivery carries these headers:

```http
POST /api/clipmux/webhook
Content-Type: application/json
X-Webhook-Event: video.asset.ready
X-Webhook-Id: evt_…
X-Webhook-Timestamp: 1800000000
X-Webhook-Signature: sha256=2efc953e06016fe9b4da70ab219f4420b381a8d5ad1a9f253f9e31da718a15d1
```

To verify one:

1. Read `X-Webhook-Timestamp` and `X-Webhook-Signature`. If either is
   missing, refuse it.
2. Check the timestamp is whole Unix seconds within 300 seconds of your
   clock, either way. This stops an old delivery being replayed.
3. Compute HMAC-SHA256 over `{timestamp}.{raw body}`: the timestamp as it
   appears in the header, a full stop, then the body's bytes. Key it with
   the whole secret, `whsec_` prefix included, as bytes.
4. Compare `sha256=` followed by the lowercase hex of that HMAC with the
   header, in constant time.

If any step fails, answer `400` and ignore the body. If they pass, parse
the body as JSON.

The timestamp is fresh on every try, so a retried delivery has a new
timestamp and signature but the same `X-Webhook-Id`.

## The raw body

The signature covers the body byte for byte. Parse it and serialize it
again, and spacing or key order changes, so the signature no longer
matches. Read the raw body before anything parses it:

- **Next.js, Hono, Bun, Deno, Workers:** `await req.text()` or
  `await req.arrayBuffer()` on the `Request`.
- **Express:** mount the webhook route before `express.json()`, or give it
  `express.raw({ type: '*/*' })`. A route after `express.json()` gets an
  object, and the signature can't match.
- **PHP:** `file_get_contents('php://input')`.

## Verify

<Tabs items={['Node', 'Python', 'Go', 'PHP']}>
<Tab value="Node">

```ts title="webhook.ts"
import { ClipMux, WebhookVerificationError } from '@clipmux/node'

const clipmux = new ClipMux() // reads CLIPMUX_WEBHOOK_SECRET

export async function POST(req: Request) {
  try {
    const event = await clipmux.webhooks.verify(await req.text(), req.headers)
    // event.type, event.data.id, …
  } catch (err) {
    if (err instanceof WebhookVerificationError) return new Response(err.reason, { status: 400 })
    throw err
  }
  return new Response(null, { status: 200 })
}
```

`verify` takes the body as a string, `Uint8Array` or `ArrayBuffer`, and the
headers as a `Headers` object or a Node headers record. It throws a
`WebhookVerificationError` whose `reason` is `missing_header`, `stale`,
`bad_signature` or `invalid_body`. `verifyWebhook(secret, rawBody, headers)`
is the same without a client.

</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">

<include cwd lang="python" meta='title="verify_webhook.py"'>snippets/python/verify_webhook.py</include>

Pass the raw body as bytes, such as `request.get_data()` in Flask or
`await request.body()` in FastAPI, and the request's headers.

</Tab>
<Tab value="Go">

<include cwd lang="go" meta='title="verify_webhook.go"'>snippets/go/verify_webhook.go</include>

Read the body with `io.ReadAll(r.Body)`, call
`VerifyWebhook(secret, body, r.Header, time.Now())`, and unmarshal the body
only when it returns `nil`.

</Tab>
<Tab value="PHP">

<include cwd lang="php" meta='title="verify_webhook.php"'>snippets/php/verify_webhook.php</include>

Call it with `file_get_contents('php://input')` and the
`X-Webhook-Timestamp` and `X-Webhook-Signature` headers, which PHP puts in
`$_SERVER['HTTP_X_WEBHOOK_TIMESTAMP']` and
`$_SERVER['HTTP_X_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE']`.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

Don't write your own if one of these fits: the comparison must be constant
time, and the timestamp check matters as much as the HMAC.

## Test against the vectors

ClipMux publishes test vectors, the cases its own server, Node SDK and the
snippets above are tested against:
[`internal/webhooks/testdata/vectors.json`](https://github.com/visheshgubrani/clipmux/blob/main/internal/webhooks/testdata/vectors.json).
Each case gives a `secret`, a clock (`now`), a `body` and the `headers`,
with whether it should verify (`valid`) and, when not, the `reason`. Run
your verifier over every case with your clock set to `now`; it must give
the same answers.

## During a secret rotation

While you rotate a secret, deliveries are signed with the old secret until
you activate the new one, then with the new one. Your verifier should accept
either for that time: try the new secret, and if the signature doesn't
match, try the old one. See
[Retries, redelivery and secret rotation](/docs/build/webhooks/retries).

## Check it works

Forward real events to your handler with `listen`, which signs them with
your `CLIPMUX_WEBHOOK_SECRET`:

```bash
npx @clipmux/node listen --forward-to localhost:3000/api/clipmux/webhook --since 10m
```

Each forwarded event prints your handler's status. `200` means it verified.
`400` means it didn't:

- `bad_signature`: the handler's secret isn't the one `listen` signs with,
  or the body was parsed before you verified it.
- `stale`: your machine's clock is more than 5 minutes off.
- `missing_header`: a proxy in front of your app dropped the headers.
